249.h: Edo State University Uzairue (EDSU) is a public university owned by the Edo State Government, founded in 2016. It is a co-educational university recognised by the National Universities Commission.
249.a: EDSU offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes across several fields, including medicine and health sciences, engineering and the sciences.
249.c: The campus is at Iyamho, near Auchi, in the Etsako West area of northern Edo State.

250.h: Edusoko University is a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission, with 2021 recorded as its year of establishment. It describes its mission as learning and discovery that drive social progress and inclusive growth in the communities it serves.
250.a: As a young university, Edusoko offers a developing range of undergraduate programmes.
250.c: The university is located in Bida, Niger State, in north-central Nigeria.

251.h: Ekiti State University, Ado-Ekiti (EKSU) is a public university owned by the Ekiti State Government. It was founded on 30 March 1982 as Obafemi Awolowo University, Ado-Ekiti, by the administration of Michael Adekunle Ajasin, the first civilian governor of the old Ondo State. Few Nigerian universities have changed name so often: it became Ondo State University in 1985, University of Ado-Ekiti in November 1999 after Ekiti State was created, and later took its present name.
251.a: EKSU offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, and is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities.
251.c: The university is located in Ado-Ekiti, the capital of Ekiti State.

252.h: Eko University of Medicine and Health Sciences (EkoUNIMED) is a private university established in 2017. It was the first private university in West Africa devoted entirely to medicine and health sciences.
252.a: The university's flagship programme is the MBBS medical degree, offered alongside BSc degrees in allied health disciplines. It received full accreditation from the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria in 2024.
252.c: The campus is at Ijanikin in Lagos State, on the Badagry road west of Lagos.

253.h: Elizade University is a private university founded by Michael Ade Ojo, the businessman behind the Elizade motor company, from which it takes its name. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2012. It began teaching in January 2013 with 64 students, 13 programmes and two faculties.
253.a: Elizade now has five faculties, Engineering, Social and Management Sciences, Basic and Applied Sciences, Law, and Humanities, with 24 departments between them.
253.c: The campus is at Ilara-Mokin in Ondo State, near Akure.

254.h: Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) is a public university owned by the Enugu State Government. It was founded on 30 July 1980 by Jim Nwobodo, then governor of the old Anambra State. When Enugu State was created out of Anambra State in 1991, the university was renamed and moved to Enugu. The National Universities Commission records 1982.
254.a: ESUT offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in science, technology, medicine, law, management and other fields.
254.c: The university is in Enugu, the capital of Enugu State in south-eastern Nigeria.

255.h: Evangel University, Akaeze is a private Christian university affiliated with the Assemblies of God church. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2012. It follows a Pentecostal tradition, and students take part in chapel services and courses in Bible and Christian service, although students from all Christian backgrounds are admitted.
255.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
255.c: It is located at Akaeze in Ebonyi State, south-eastern Nigeria.

256.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB) is owned and run by the Federal Government of Nigeria. The National Universities Commission lists 1988 as its year of establishment, when it became one of the federal government's specialised universities of agriculture.
256.a: FUNAAB specialises in agriculture and related sciences, such as animal science, crop production, food science, forestry and veterinary medicine, alongside the basic sciences and engineering.
256.c: The university is located in Abeokuta, the capital of Ogun State.

258.h: The Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun (FUPRE) was approved by the Federal Executive Council on 14 March 2007 and admitted its first undergraduates in 2008. It was created as a specialised university in the Niger Delta to train professionals for the oil and gas industry. In its early years the National Universities Commission allowed it to share facilities with the Petroleum Training Institute in Effurun while its main campus was developed.
258.a: FUPRE's programmes focus on petroleum engineering, geosciences, and other engineering and science disciplines relevant to the energy sector.
258.c: The university is located in Effurun, near Warri, Delta State.

259.h: The Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) is a federal university established by the Federal Government of Nigeria in 1981, during the period when the government set up universities of technology in several regions.
259.a: FUTA concentrates on engineering, technology, the sciences, agriculture and environmental studies.
259.c: The university is located in Akure, the capital of Ondo State.

260.h: The Federal University of Technology, Minna (FUTMinna) is a federal university that specialises in technological education. Wikipedia gives 1983 for its establishment, while the National Universities Commission records 1982. Its first vice-chancellor, Professor J. O. Ndagi, served from 1983 to 1990.
260.a: The university offers bachelor's and master's degrees in technology-related fields. It is a designated Centre of Excellence in Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering, with research on vaccines and drugs, and it has worked with the Nigerian armed forces on small arms design.
260.c: FUTMinna is located in Minna, the capital of Niger State.

261.h: The Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO) was the first federal university of technology in Nigeria. It was established in 1980 by Shehu Shagari, Nigeria's first executive president, as part of a plan to set up a university of technology in each geopolitical region and so support the country's technological development.
261.a: FUTO's programmes centre on engineering, technology, the physical and life sciences, agriculture and health technology.
261.c: The campus is in Owerri West, near Owerri, the capital of Imo State, and is bounded by the communities of Eziobodo, Ihiagwa, Obinze, Okolochi and Emeabiam.

262.h: Federal University, Birnin Kebbi (FUBK) was established on 18 February 2013, at the same time as the federal universities in Gusau and Gashua, under President Goodluck Jonathan. They were created under the government's policy of giving a federal university to each state that did not already have one.
262.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
262.c: It is located in Birnin Kebbi, the capital of Kebbi State in north-western Nigeria.

263.h: Federal University, Dutse (FUD) is a federal university founded in 2011 as one of the nine federal universities created that year to widen access to university education. It is a co-educational institution recognised by the National Universities Commission.
263.a: FUD offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and health sciences.
263.c: The university is located in Dutse, the capital of Jigawa State.

264.h: Federal University, Dutsin-Ma (FUDMA) was founded in February 2011 by the administration of President Goodluck Jonathan, as one of the nine new federal universities created that year. It began full operations in 2012.
264.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
264.c: It is located in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in north-western Nigeria.

265.h: Federal University, Gashua (FUGashua) is a public university established in February 2013 under the Federal Government's programme to expand access to higher education in states without a federal university.
265.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is developing its range of courses under a five-year development plan.
265.c: It is located in Gashua, Yobe State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

266.h: Federal University, Gusau (FUGUS) was one of twelve new federal universities proposed in 2010. Nine were opened in February 2011, and Gusau was among the remaining three, established in 2013 under President Goodluck Jonathan.
266.a: The university started with three faculties: Humanities and Education, Management and Social Sciences, and Science.
266.c: It is located in Gusau, the capital of Zamfara State.

267.h: Federal University, Kashere (FUKashere) is a federal university established in 2011, one of the nine new federal universities created that year to give more states a federal university.
267.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
267.c: It is located in Kashere, Gombe State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

268.h: Federal University of Lafia (FULafia) is a federal university established on 9 February 2011 by the government of President Goodluck Jonathan, as one of nine new federal universities. They were created to widen access to university education and ease the pressure on existing universities.
268.a: FULafia offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
268.c: The university is located in Lafia, the capital of Nasarawa State.

269.h: Federal University, Lokoja (FUL) was established by the Federal Government in February 2011, as one of nine new federal universities created to meet demand for university places.
269.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
269.c: It has two campuses in Lokoja, the capital of Kogi State: the permanent campus at Felele and another at Adankolo. Lokoja lies where the Niger and Benue rivers meet.

270.h: Federal University, Otuoke (FUOtuoke) is one of the nine federal universities established in February 2011 under President Goodluck Jonathan. It started with 282 pioneer students.
270.a: The university has six faculties and offers undergraduate degrees and postgraduate diplomas, master's degrees and doctorates.
270.c: It is in Otuoke, a town in the Ogbia local government area of Bayelsa State, in the oil-producing Niger Delta.

271.h: Federal University, Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) is a federal university founded in 2011 as one of nine new federal universities created that year. It is a co-educational institution recognised by the National Universities Commission.
271.a: FUOYE offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and engineering.
271.c: The main campus is at Oye-Ekiti, with a second campus at Ikole, both in Ekiti State.
